Ben / Marissa / Lauren — thanks, here’s a concise validation plan and GPU comparison summary we can run within the Feb 16–18 window. I’ll own execution with ops support.

High-level approach (3 phases)
Phase 0 — Warmup & baseline (4–6 hours)
- Run hosted Redwood model baseline on a medium synthetic workload to validate test harness and reproduce token latency distributions.
- Verify profiling (kernel timelines, KV cache misses).

Phase 1 — Dedicated baseline (A100 vs H100) (1.5 days)
- Provision two small dedicated clusters: A100-80GB and H100-80GB, single-card per-node pools to measure single-GPU latencies, and 4x-card pools for throughput scaling.
- Metrics: token P50/P95/P99, end-to-end request P95, throughput at fixed concurrency, GPU utilization, kv-cache hit rates.
- Streaming behavior: measure token emission latency and jitter under prefix caching.

Phase 2 — Cost-focused variant (L4 / quantized path) + spike tests (0.5 day)
- Run L4 (or equivalent) configuration with int8/quantized model path to capture cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Execute short spike test to 1,200 concurrency and validate graceful degradation: fallback routing to smaller model or queueing policy.

GPU comparison summary (quick)
- H100: best raw throughput and lower token tail latency for long sequences; higher cost per hour. Good if your SLOs are strict for long transcripts.
- A100 (80GB): balanced — strong throughput with better cost efficiency in many streaming cases; solid default recommendation if you need both streaming latency and throughput consistency.
- L4/quantized: cost-efficient for lower-latency short-turn interactions, but watch tail behavior for long transcripts (quantization degrades long-context latency and quality in some models).

Reserved throughput recommendation (draft)
- Baseline reserved throughput: 60 req/s (covers steady 600–800 concurrency with average token lengths).
- Burst reserve/burst window: provision burst capacity up to 150% (90 req/s) for 10–15 minute windows to absorb spikes; rely on autoscaling fallback to handle longer spikes with degraded SLOs.

Deliverables (by Feb 19 EOD)
- Perf report with graphs + GPU recommendation matrix
- Sizing sheet with reserved throughput numbers and expected cost ranges
- Short runbook for autoscaling, fallback policies, and procurement notes for Private deployment/KMS requirements.

Data we need from SynthMed ASAP
- Finalized prompt set (anonymized) — they already attached v1, good starting point.
- Representative concurrency distribution file if available (a 1-week CSV of request timestamps is ideal).

I’ll draft perf-test-specs.md and upload to the Drive link; Ben, can you confirm the HubSpot deal and give ops permission to provision the clusters?
